name: Argentina
style_description: Tactically disciplined and structured, Argentina blend defensive solidity with devastating counter-attacking pace through their wide channels. Messi acts as a free-roaming creative hub in a low block that absorbs pressure before exploding forward in transition, with De Paul providing relentless energy in midfield to bridge defense and attack.

name: France
style_description: France possess the most lethal counter-attacking threat in world football, built around Mbappe's devastating pace and clinical finishing. Deschamps deploys a compact mid-block that suffocates opponents before releasing Mbappe and Griezmann on the break, with Tchouameni anchoring a physically imposing midfield that rarely concedes space.

name: Spain
style_description: Spain are the purest possession team in modern football, building from the back with intricate short passing sequences that suffocate opponents by dominating the ball for long stretches. Their press is immediate and positionally coordinated, while Yamal's explosive dribbling on the right wing adds unpredictable direct threat to an otherwise methodical system.

name: England
style_description: England operate in a flexible 4-2-3-1 that prioritises width and crossing into Kane, with Bellingham given freedom to arrive late in the box as a secondary attacking threat. They are defensively compact and difficult to break down, though their build-up play through the thirds can be overly direct and predictable against deep-lying opposition.

name: Brazil
style_description: High-intensity attacking football with technical flair, quick combinations, and creative individual play define Brazil's identity. Vinicius Jr provides constant menace on the left wing with explosive dribbling and directness, while the team's natural rhythm in tight spaces allows them to unlock even deep defensive blocks through improvisation and individual moments of brilliance.

name: Portugal
style_description: Portugal mix direct attacking intent with patient possession phases, built around Ronaldo's penalty-box presence and Fernandes' creative playmaking from deep. Martinez has constructed a system that channels the ball quickly into wide areas before delivering crosses and cutbacks, supported by Dias marshalling a physically strong and well-organised defensive block.

name: Belgium
style_description: Belgium are a direct, powerful side that relies on De Bruyne's elite passing range to find Lukaku in advanced positions and break opposition lines with a single incisive ball. Their shape is compact defensively and expansive in attack, using wide areas to create crossing opportunities for Lukaku's physical dominance in the penalty area.

name: Switzerland
style_description: Switzerland are a tactically disciplined and well-drilled side that excels at frustrating technically superior opponents through a compact defensive shape and intelligent pressing triggers. Xhaka dictates the tempo from deep midfield with precise short passing, and the team is adept at transitioning quickly from defence to attack through direct vertical balls to wide runners.

name: Netherlands
style_description: The Netherlands play an aggressive, high-pressing style rooted in Total Football tradition, with van Dijk organising a high defensive line that squeezes opponents into their own half. Wide players cut inside to create numerical overloads in central areas, while Simons operates as a creative link between midfield and attack with sharp passing and intelligent movement.

name: Germany
style_description: Germany under Nagelsmann have rediscovered their attacking identity, pressing aggressively high and transitioning at speed through Musiala and Wirtz — two of world football's most dynamic creative midfielders who combine technical dexterity with relentless work rate. Their system is fluid rather than rigid, allowing positional interchange between attack and midfield lines to create unpredictable overloads.

name: Croatia
style_description: Croatia are a tactically mature, possession-based side whose midfield triumvirate of Modric, Kovacic, and Brozovic has long been the finest ball-controlling unit in international football. They dominate games through relentless passing recycling and intelligent positional play, growing stronger as matches progress and excelling in the high-pressure knockout environments where their experience proves decisive.

name: Uruguay
style_description: Under Bielsa, Uruguay have adopted an intense pressing game with high defensive lines and aggressive recovery runs that demand extraordinary fitness from every player. Valverde's box-to-box dynamism is central to both pressing phases and attacking transitions, while Nunez's raw pace and physical power up front gives the team a direct and threatening outlet when winning the ball high up the pitch.

name: Italy
style_description: Italy blend their legendary defensive tradition with a modern pressing game and rapid attacking transitions, with Barella's intense box-to-box energy as the engine of Spalletti's system. They are difficult to break down due to excellent defensive shape and Donnarumma's commanding goalkeeping, while Chiesa's pace and directness on the wing provides the main outlet for quick counters.

name: Denmark
style_description: Denmark are a compact, well-organised side that presses with intensity in the middle third before using Eriksen's precise distribution to quickly move the ball forward to Hojlund. Their collective work ethic and mutual defensive responsibility gives them a resilience that makes them uncomfortable opponents for any team, and set pieces from Eriksen provide a consistent threat throughout matches.

name: Morocco
style_description: Morocco are built on extraordinary defensive organisation and collective industry, using a low block that is almost impossible to break down through central areas, forcing teams wide before winning the second ball. Hakimi's overlapping runs from right wing-back are their primary attacking mechanism, while Ziyech's creativity and ability to deliver precise set-piece deliveries adds a clinical edge.
weaknesses: Attacking creativity without Ziyech at peak

name: Colombia
style_description: Colombia play a high-energy, wide-attacking game with Diaz and Cuadrado providing constant width and directness to stretch opposition defensive lines. James Rodriguez operates as the creative hub, threading through balls and dictating tempo from a free midfield role, while their pressing triggers in the middle third are well-drilled and efficient at recovering possession quickly.

name: Mexico
style_description: Mexico are a technically gifted, possession-oriented side who build patiently from the back through their comfortable centre-backs before using the creativity of Lozano and wide midfielders to unlock defensive lines. Alvarez provides the defensive backbone in a midfield pivot, and the team's positional fluidity in attack allows multiple players to drift into dangerous areas around the penalty box.

name: United States
style_description: Pochettino's USA are a high-pressing, energetic side with excellent athleticism and physical conditioning that allows them to maintain defensive intensity throughout matches. Pulisic is the creative fulcrum and primary threat, capable of carrying the ball past defenders and delivering in the final third, while Adams' combative midfield work provides the platform for the attacking players to express themselves.

name: Canada
style_description: Canada under Marsch play an intense, physically demanding game with a high defensive line and aggressive pressing triggers designed to win the ball in dangerous areas. Davies' explosive pace and attacking quality from left back creates a constant overload on that side, while David's intelligent off-the-ball movement and clinical finishing up front makes them a genuine goal threat from limited opportunities.

name: Senegal
style_description: Senegal are built on raw athleticism, physical power, and direct attacking intent centred around Mane's ability to take on defenders in one-vs-one situations anywhere across the front line. Their defensive shape is anchored by Koulibaly's commanding presence and Mendy's reliable shot-stopping, and they are a formidable set-piece team who use their height and strength to threaten from dead balls in both boxes.

name: Japan
style_description: Japan are a compact, tactically astute side who operate in a well-drilled 4-2-3-1 that prioritises defensive shape before unleashing technically sharp attacking combinations through the lines. Their press is intelligent and coordinated rather than purely physical, and Kubo's creativity in the number ten role provides imagination to unlock deep defences with quick one-two exchanges and sharp dribbling in tight spaces.

name: South Korea
style_description: South Korea channel the ball into Son Heung-min in wide positions as quickly as possible, relying on his elite movement off the ball and devastating finishing to create and convert chances from fast transitions. Kim Min-jae anchors a physical and aggressive defensive unit, and the team as a whole works with exceptional energy and collective discipline, particularly effective at funnelling opponents into defensive situations before breaking at pace.

name: Australia
style_description: Australia play an honest, physically demanding brand of football that relies on excellent fitness levels, direct forward play, and intense pressing to disrupt technically superior opponents. Their long-throw and set-piece delivery is a genuine weapon, and they are masters of exploiting opponents who underestimate their physical intensity, using McGree's energy in central midfield to create turnovers in dangerous areas.

name: Ecuador
style_description: Ecuador blend physical directness with growing technical sophistication, built around Caicedo's exceptional midfield control and ball-winning ability that provides the platform for the attack. Enner Valencia's experience and aerial presence up front gives them a focal point, while the exciting emergence of Kendry Paez as a technically brilliant attacking midfielder adds creativity and unpredictability to their attacking play.

name: Serbia
style_description: Serbia are a physically imposing, direct side who build their entire attacking strategy around delivering quality service to their twin striker threat of Mitrovic and Vlahovic — two of world football's most clinical and physical centre-forwards. Milinkovic-Savic provides dynamic box-to-box energy and late runs into the area, while their set-piece delivery from wide positions is consistently dangerous given their aerial dominance.

name: Poland
style_description: Poland's system is constructed entirely around maximising Lewandowski's goal-scoring output, with Zielinski delivering precise through balls and the wide players cutting inside to create space for the striker's intelligent runs. They are defensively solid and disciplined, sitting in a compact shape that frustrates opponents and relies on Lewandowski's individual brilliance to turn limited chances into decisive goals.

name: Nigeria
style_description: Nigeria are an explosive, athletically outstanding side who use Osimhen's extraordinary pace, strength, and finishing ability as their primary attacking weapon in a fast-breaking, direct system. Lookman's creativity and ability to drift inside from wide positions provides an important secondary threat, while the team's sheer physical gifts make them dangerous in transition and capable of beating any opponent on their day.

name: Cameroon
style_description: Cameroon are a physically powerful side with excellent individual athletes across the pitch, using direct and pacey wide attackers to stretch defensive lines before delivering into a physically dominant striker. Onana's distribution from goal is an important outlet to bypass the press, and their ability to compete physically with any opponent makes them a threat particularly in aerial duels and physical second-ball contests.

name: Ghana
style_description: Ghana play an energetic, direct, and wide-attacking game that uses the individual brilliance of Kudus to create moments of magic in tight spaces between defensive lines. Their pressing is enthusiastic and physical, with Kudus also contributing significantly off the ball, and Semenyo's direct running and crossing from the right wing provides a complementary wide threat to Kudus' creative work on the opposite flank.

name: Iran
style_description: Iran are an extremely well-organised, disciplined side who defend in a deep and compact low block that is designed to frustrate possession-based teams and limit space in behind. Taremi is one of world football's most underrated forwards, combining clever movement, technical quality, and a combative work rate that presses defenders into mistakes, while Azmoun provides a physically imposing alternative attacking option.

name: Saudi Arabia
style_description: Under Mancini, Saudi Arabia have adopted a more tactically sophisticated style with a higher defensive line and coordinated pressing triggers than their previous iterations. Al-Dawsari is their primary creative and goal threat, with the ability to cut inside from the left and shoot with either foot, while Al-Owais has established himself as one of Asia's finest goalkeepers and is capable of single-handedly keeping them competitive against stronger opponents.

name: New Zealand
style_description: New Zealand are a pragmatic, hardworking side who make up for their lack of elite technical quality with exceptional collective organisation, high work-rate across all 90 minutes, and a direct aerial game built around Chris Wood's powerful hold-up play and finishing. They are physically robust and genuinely difficult to break down for any opponent willing to underestimate their determination and tactical discipline.
